tutor.step.fux-mode.s1.01.intro: [Placeholder] Aloysius sets the first cantus firmus and asks Josephus to write a counterpoint above it, note against note.
tutor.result.cleared: [Placeholder] Aloysius approves: no rule is broken.
tutor.result.notCleared: [Placeholder] Aloysius points out what must be corrected.
tutor.rule.fs.vertical-consonance: [Placeholder] Only consonances are allowed in this species; this interval is a dissonance.
tutor.rule.fs.opening-perfect: [Placeholder] Begin with a perfect consonance (with the counterpoint below: the octave or unison, to stay in the mode).
tutor.rule.fs.final-octave-or-unison: [Placeholder] End on the octave or the unison.
tutor.rule.fs.cadence: [Placeholder] Before the final, the cantus below asks for a major sixth (the cantus above, a minor third), opening to the octave.
tutor.rule.fs.perfect-approach: [Placeholder] A perfect consonance may be reached only by contrary or oblique motion.
tutor.rule.fs.unison-only-at-ends: [Placeholder] The unison belongs only at the beginning and the end.
tutor.rule.fs.melodic-tritone: [Placeholder] Mi against fa: the leap of a tritone is forbidden.
tutor.rule.fs.melodic-major-sixth: [Placeholder] The leap of a major sixth is forbidden.
tutor.rule.fs.converging-leap-into-octave: [Placeholder] Do not leap into the octave or unison from a distant consonance with the voices converging.
tutor.rule.fs.unison-leap: [Placeholder] Do not leap out of, or into, the unison.
tutor.rule.fs.no-voice-crossing: [Placeholder] Here the counterpoint crosses the cantus firmus.
tutor.rule.fs.prefer-contrary-motion: [Placeholder] Use contrary or oblique motion as much as possible; here similar motion predominates.
